test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 27 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Identify the type of the following sentence from the passage:

"Each region contributes a unique weaving style: such as Chanderi, Pochampally Ikat, and Kanjeevaram, reflecting the stories, rituals, and environments of its people."
solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 1: Simple sentence***

 
 
• A **simple sentence** contains only one independent clause. An independent clause has a subject and a verb and expresses a complete thought.
 
• In the given sentence, the subject is "Each region" and the verb is "contributes." Even though the sentence is long and contains lists and phrases, it only has one main subject-verb pair forming a single independent clause.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Compound sentence***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. A compound sentence must have at least two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction (like and, but, or) or a semicolon. There is no second independent clause here.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Complex sentence***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. A complex sentence requires one independent clause and at least one dependent (subordinate) clause. The phrase starting with "reflecting" is a **participle phrase**, not a clause, because it does not have its own subject and finite verb.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Compound-complex sentence***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. This type requires at least two independent clauses and one or more dependent clauses. This sentence meets neither requirement.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Clause vs. Phrase**: It is easy to confuse long phrases with clauses. A clause must have a **finite verb** (a verb that shows tense). "Reflecting" is a present participle (non-finite), so it forms a phrase that modifies the noun "style," not a new clause.
 
• **The Role of Colons**: The colon in this sentence is used to introduce a list of examples. It does not separate two different clauses, so it doesn't change the sentence type.
